Effects of estrogen: During the menstruation, the level of estrogen is too low to maintain the endometrium, causing its functional layer to shed.
Effects of progesterone: The level of progesterone is too low to maintain the endometrium stable, causing it to shed.
Effects of FSH: During menstruation, the level of FSH is low but rising because GnRH is released by the hypothalamus, triggering the production of FSH by the anterior pituitary. This stimulates the development of several ovarian follicles.
Effects of LH: The level of LH is low during menstruation but increases gradually as hypothalamus releases GnRH which triggers the anterior pituitary to release LH.
Energy Levels Text: You might be experiencing low energy and tiredness. This time calls for rest and recovery and gentle exercises.
Type of food: Eat foods containing iron to prevent  anemia and eat foods with vitamin B to provide energy. Some examples of foods to eat are red meat, poultry, fish, legumes,nuts and seeds and leafy greens.
Example of Food: For further information on the types of food and recipes you can make dependent on the phase you are in,you can find it here. https://elara.care/nutrition/menstrual-cycle-food-chart/#mid-luteal-phase-foods
Concentration Levels: Through this phase you might feel a difference on how well you can process information, as well as having harder time memorizing and lower attention. This is due to the lower amounts of estrogen levels.
Health aspect: The average menstrual phase is 5 days, however this can vary depending on the person. This variation may alter the length of your menstrual cycle. If your overall cycle is longer than 35 days that can be a sign of  or shorter than 21 days. If you have concerns, contact your doctor.
Types of Vitamins: While on your period you can take iron supplements to make up for the iron lost in blood and to prevent fatigue. Magesium can be taken to support your muscles and also lower fatigue. Additionally Vitamin C can be taken to support iron absorption for inflamation and fatigue prevention. Before taking any supplements, please contact your doctor.
What is happening in the Brain: Hypothalamus releases GnRH (gonadotropin-releasing hormone) which stimulates the anterior pituitary to produce FSH and LH.
What is happening in the Ovaries: Rising level of FSH stimulates the development of several ovarian follicles. No dominant follicle is yet observable, they are all competing.
What is happening in the Uterus: The low amount of estrogens and progesterones cannot maintain the stability of the endometrium anymore, causing the uterine lining to shed blood and tissues : this is the menstrual flow.
What is happening in each phase: It is the start of a new menstrual cycle. The body re-prepares itself for a future possible fertilization : the lining of the uterus is shed through the vagina and ovarian follicles start their development.
